title: Bechet on the Smoky Mary, continued
summary: Dawson repeats how he fetched sleeping Bechet from the train and sobered him up for the picnic; Bechet could really play.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: You were talking about Sidney Maché going to the street there, going back?

Yeah, and they'd send me out there to go catch the train when it'd blow, it'd blow, you know. We'd be well over there in the camp. All the men, we done played a couple of numbers already waiting. I'd go out there and ask the conductor and fix him to go back and sit. I'd say, you seen a fellow musician? There's a fellow up there in the seat there, he'd been sleeping. We'd brought him back to town about three times. He'd go back there and say, get up here, bitch, get up. Pull him up, get his horn, and bring him outside and bring him to one of them ballrooms right across from, you know, and make him wash his face, you know, straighten up, get him a wine, and give him a fresh wine, and he'd come on back out to that picnic, that camp, and blow that thing. I mean, he could blow.
Really good then, he was pretty young then, I guess.
Yes, indeed, he could play. He looked like nothing wouldn't happen to him, but he just like that. Yes, sir.
